title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep anchor round 2 — expression-editors' RLS clauses to the engine's error tier, a consumed-changeset citation, and §3 accuracy corrections in five areas
body:
Refs #24579

Clause-②: no

Part of #24579: the wave anchor's second dispatch (round 1, #24622, landed §1's five rows). This PR lands three parts: (a) the §1 row round 2 added, (b) the rider from the #24622 review, and (c) §3's checklist-accuracy findings for platform-core, access-security, attachments-storage, identity-auth and approvals. The card stays open for §2, §4, the other areas' §3 bullets and round 2's other additions.

The diff edits checklist content only (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/`, seven files). No product code, test or pin changes. Every finding below was re-derived from source at the base `8fbbd5082f` (and, for console claims, objectui at the console pin `4016370a`) before the item was edited. A finding that did not hold is in the left-alone list with the reading that refuted it. Each edited item takes one `revision` bump and one `history` row that names its run record(s) and carries this PR as `ref`. Several findings on one item make one revision.

## (a) §1 — the round-2 row

| item | fields edited | revision | run record |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `studio-authoring.expression-editors` | `acceptance[2].clause`, `acceptance[2].verify`, `acceptance[4].clause`, `acceptance[4].evidence`, `acceptance[4].verify`, `fixtures.knownGaps[3]` (added), `steps[0]`, `steps[4]`, `variants[2]` | 3 → 4 | #24604, #24571 |

acceptance[2] and acceptance[4] required a non-pushdownable USING read filter to be an advisory WARNING with Save enabled and fail-open framing. The engine refuses that predicate at ERROR tier: `packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts` emits `rls-predicate-unenforceable` with severity `error` (ADR-0056 D4), the rule `os build` and publish run, and the runtime fails CLOSED (the dropped policy grants no access). negative[0] already fails any editor verdict that differs from the engine, so the item contradicted itself (#24604 scored acceptance[4] "pass (as written)" beside a negative[0] FAIL). Both clauses now expect the error tier. Four more fields ride the same re-point so the item stays consistent:
- steps[4] and variants[2] expect the error tier.
- steps[0] names the build/publish gate as the RLS probes' engine truth, because `validate_expression` has no RLS site.
- acceptance[4] names the Studio package door's autosave-held status beside the environment door's disabled Save (#24604: the package door has no Save button).
- A new knownGap records that at the console pin the editor still warns (objectui `celAuthoring.ts` `lintCelPredicate`). The clauses therefore FAIL until objectstack-ai/objectui#13061 lands.

## (b) the #24622 rider

| item | fields edited | revision | run record |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `cli.organization-ownership-ceremony` | `source`: the path entry `.changeset/pre/15212-180-guards-fresh-single-only.md` removed, `15212-180-guards-fresh-single-only` appended to the prose entry "v18 changesets (.changeset/pre/, consumed into 18.0.0-next.*): …" | 2 (unchanged — no history row) | the #24622 review |

The path entry dangles once 18.0.0 is versioned, because the version render consumes `.changeset/pre/*.md`. Ledger rule, measured: `check:platform-checklist` requires only `revision` equal to the last `history` row's revision, and the README bumps "on any semantic edit", meaning one that would let an old run result read as valid against changed clauses. A citation fold changes no clause, step or fixture a run judges, and this item already took a revision today for #24622, so no revision and no history row. Counter-reading, for the record: the ledger has bumped for a source-only addition before (`platform-core.boot-health`, its "source-ref addition" row). If the seat reads the rule that way, the fix is a revision-3 row naming this PR. The item's `fixtures.knownGaps[0]` prose also names `.changeset/pre/15212-180-guards-fresh-single-only.md` in a sentence, and that mention was left as it is: the ruling names the source entry only.

## Findings left alone, each with the reading that refuted or excluded it

- `platform-core.boot-health`, round 2's "the check-console-injection replay line still says 'not the published one'": no area file carries a check-console-injection line. At the base, a search of all 16 area files for `check-console-injection`, `console-injection` and `published one` finds zero matches. The sentence is the output of `scripts/check-console-injection.mjs` (its success line), which is product text and outside this checklist-only ruling.
- `platform-core.settings-hub-roundtrip` (`value_domain`; no user-scoped namespace): excluded, because open PR #24590 holds the item.
- `platform-core.settings-organization-isolation-and-platform-rung`, plus the walled legs of `access-security.walled-environment-metadata-operator-only`, `activation-write-operator-gate`, `grant-table-write-contract` acceptance[4] and `parent-and-organization-write-guards`: §2 (walled posture), so not this round. The record's "the minimal object body must declare sharingModel" note sits on `walled-environment-metadata-operator-only` steps[0], a walled-boot step, and is left for that item's §2 revision.
- `platform-core.metadata-authoring-roundtrip` (the objectui `studio-record-page` / `studio-object-designer` specs are red at their own pin): §2's "objectui live e2e is not green at its pin" theme.

- `attachments-storage.chunked-upload-integrity` acceptance[1] (chunk numbering base): already corrected on main by #24622 (revision 2 numbers chunks from 0 and expects `missingChunks` [1]). Its second-organization fixture is §2.

- `access-security.capability-declaration-lifecycle`, "DELETE /api/v1/meta/capability/NAME is a 200 no-op": no clause or step asserts the DELETE door, so nothing in the item is inaccurate. The 200-that-deletes-nothing answer is a product observation and is not encoded here (see Acceptance notes).
- `attachments-storage.inline-grid-receipt-cells` (objectui-only pin scored by hand): a run-method note under RUNNER's objectui-pin protocol, not an inaccuracy.
- identity-auth, accurate as written: `auth-method-matrix` (discovery also answered under /api/v1/auth, which the record calls harmless; the item requires only the root mount) and `two-factor-enrollment-reveal` (the record calls the anonymous 400 "consistent with the clause"). `admin-lifecycle-operations`'s impersonation-banner note is a UX observation outside every clause.
- identity-auth, suggestions rather than errors: `two-factor-verify-to-activate` / `-backup-codes` / `-disable-lifecycle` ("worth naming" a SQLite-file rig as an alternative to the in-process read, which still works). `auth-gate-held-session-raw-host-families` boots with `pnpm dev -- --fresh`, AGENTS.md's documented backend-only boot.

## PM hypotheses, measured

1. **Stale findings because main moved — partly confirmed.** Diffed between run subject `5b14b7f3` and base `8fbbd5082f`, the cited sources changed in three files. `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (#24526) and `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` (#24587) changed, but not in the cited symbols (NamespaceConflictError, the org-MFA cache). `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` changed with #24527 and then #24620 (merged here); neither touches `rowFromRequest` or `comment`. Main's movement staled one finding (act-door, by #24620). Two more were already handled on main (chunked numbering and share-link ai_conversations, both by #24622). One was wrong at the base itself (boot-health).
2. **"automated.ref omits X" is a pin-coverage claim — confirmed.** Five pins were added after measurement (table above). One claim had no pin to add (chunked-upload-integrity), and the item records the gap instead.
3. **Symbol-anchor count must not drop — confirmed.** `check:platform-checklist` read 860/870 resolved at the base and 872/882 at head: 12 anchors added, none lost, the 10 on the named #16898 residual unchanged, 18 file floors held. No re-pointed anchor was refused.
